claim: Asked on June 10, 2026 why the detainees still held at Guantánamo Bay had not been put to death, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth told reporters at MacDill Air Force Base in Tampa, hours after visiting the Cuba base: "These Gitmo detainees should have been executed, in my mind, personally, a long time ago, for the crimes of what they committed against the American people." He added that "the gears of American justice got gunked up, all the way back to when I was a guard at Guantánamo Bay," and that "we're committed to the death penalty ... in that case and in any others." Fifteen men remained in the camp at the time, five of them facing capital charges before the military commissions for the September 11, 2001 attacks; the rest have never been charged.

sources.label: U.S. Department of War, "Press Gaggle With Secretary of War Pete Hegseth," MacDill Air Force Base, Tampa, Florida, June 10, 2026 (official transcript; war.gov blocks our fetcher, so the verbatim below is carried from reporting).
The Daily Beast, "Pete Hegseth Says Quiet Part Out Loud in Shocking Guantánamo Bay Remark," June 10, 2026.

notes: Quote is consistent verbatim across The Daily Beast, Al Jazeera, Ynet-syndication and DPA wire copy. Detainee count of 15 with five 9/11 co-defendants is as of June 2026 reporting. Surfaced alongside 2026-hegseth-gitmo-guard-001 and 2002-adayfi-detention-001.
